title: Minimum Number of Refueling Stops
statement:
A car drives east from position `0` toward a destination at position `target`, burning exactly one liter of fuel per mile. It begins with `startFuel` liters, and its tank has no capacity limit. Each `stations[i] = [position, fuel]` is a gas station `position` miles east of the start holding `fuel` liters; stopping there moves all of that fuel into the car.

Return the fewest stops needed to reach `target`, or `-1` if the destination cannot be reached at all. Arriving at a station or at the destination with an empty tank still counts as reaching it (and the car may refuel at that station).
signature: int minRefuelStops(int target, int startFuel, int[][] stations)
notes:
## Intuition

Think of fuel as reach: with `reach` liters burned in total the car gets exactly `reach` miles from the start. Instead of deciding at each station whether to stop, drive as far as the current fuel allows and remember every station passed. When the car would run dry, pretend, in hindsight, that it stopped at the passed station with the most fuel. Picking the largest available amount is never worse, because every station passed is equally reachable and a bigger refill pushes `reach` further. A max-heap hands out that largest amount quickly. (A slower dynamic programme tracks the farthest reach for each number of stops in O(n²).)

## Approach

1. Keep a max-heap `heap` of fuel amounts from stations already within reach, with hand-written `push` and `pop`.
2. Start with `reach = startFuel`, `stops = 0` and `next = 0`, the first station not yet considered.
3. While `reach < target`, push the fuel of every station whose position is at most `reach`.
4. If the heap is empty, no passed station can help, so return `-1`.
5. Otherwise pop the largest amount, add it to `reach` and count one stop.
6. Once `reach >= target`, return `stops`.

## Example 1, step by step

For `target = 1`, `startFuel = 1` and no stations, `reach` starts at `1`, which is not less than `target`, so the loop never runs and the answer is `0`. (In Example 3, `reach = 10` admits the station with 60, giving `reach = 70`; that admits 30, 30 and 40, and popping 40 gives `110`, so 2 stops.)

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n): each station is pushed and popped at most once, each heap operation costing O(log n).
- Space: O(n) for the heap.

## Pitfalls

- A station exactly at `reach` is reachable (the car arrives with 0 liters), so admit it with `<=`.
- Stopping greedily at the first station is wrong; delay the choice until fuel runs out, then take the biggest passed station.
- Totals can exceed 2^31 (500 stations of nearly 10^9 liters), so Java and C need a 64-bit `reach`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `heap` | max-heap of fuel from stations already passed but not used |
| `push`, `pop` | add an amount to `heap` / remove and return its largest |
| `reach` | farthest position the fuel collected so far can carry the car |
| `stops` | refuelling stops used so far |
| `next` | index of the first station not yet added to `heap` |

narration.2: The max-heap stores fuel amounts of stations the car has already passed but not used.
narration.3: push adds one fuel amount to the heap.
narration.6: Sift the new amount up while it is larger than its parent.
narration.8: The parent is at least as large, so the heap order holds again.
narration.13: pop removes and returns the largest stored amount.
narration.17: Move the last amount to the root before sifting it down.
narration.19: Sift down: swap with the larger child until both children are smaller.
narration.32: With only the starting fuel, the car can get startFuel miles.
narration.35: Keep refuelling until the collected fuel is enough to reach target.
narration.36: Every station at or before reach could have been visited, including one reached with an empty tank.
narration.37: Remember its fuel as a possible stop to make in hindsight.
narration.40: No passed station is left to use, so the car is stuck short of target.
narration.41: Use the passed station with the most fuel: it extends reach the furthest.
narration.42: That counts as one refuelling stop.
narration.44: reach covers target, so this is the fewest stops.
